subject: Architecture
title: Art Nouveau: When Buildings Grew Vines
description: Learn Art Nouveau: When Buildings Grew Vines in one minute.

hook.text: Around 1890, architects decided buildings should look like nature — curves, vines, and flowers.

buildup.text: Art Nouveau rejected straight lines. Iron was bent into whiplash curves mimicking plant stems.

discovery.text: Hector Guimard's Paris Métro entrances look like giant iron plants growing from the sidewalk.

twist.text: Every piece was custom-made. Mass production killed the style because it was too expensive.

climax.text: Antoni Gaudí pushed Art Nouveau furthest — his buildings in Barcelona look almost alive.

punchline.text: They built nature from iron and glass. Then the factories made it extinct.

quiz.question: What ultimately killed the Art Nouveau movement?
options: A shift in public taste toward classical styles
Custom craftsmanship was too expensive for mass production
